prompt: According to the lesson, what does a forecast consist of?
hint: More than the number Otávio asked for.

choices.text: One number, as precise as the data allows
choices.why: That is the wrong idea the lesson opens with: one number hides how wrong it may be.

choices.text: A number and the method that produced it, with the formula written out
choices.why: The method matters, but without a range the reader still cannot tell how far to trust it.

choices.text: A number, a horizon and a range
choices.why: Right: the range tells the person deciding how much weight the number can carry.

choices.text: A best case and a worst case, with no middle
choices.why: Lívia gave a middle too: R$ 22.0 million, between 21.5 and 22.5.

prompt: Made at the end of June 2025, each method forecast December 2025 differently. Match each method to its forecast, in thousands of reais.
hint: June 2025 was 7,330 and December 2024 was 11,290.

pairs.left: Seasonal naive: the same month a year before
Seasonal naive × the first half's growth

prompt: Why did Lívia send Otávio "between 21.5 and 22.5 million" rather than "22.0 million" alone?
hint: What does Otávio do with it?

choices.text: To protect herself if the quarter came in lower
choices.why: The range is for the decision, not for the analyst.

choices.text: So he could plan for a miss before it happened
choices.why: Right: a miss nobody announced cannot be planned for.

choices.text: Because the spreadsheet cannot compute a single number for three months
choices.why: It computed one: 22,010. The range is added to it.

choices.text: Because a CFO is required to report ranges to the bank
choices.why: The lesson gives no such rule; the reason is what the range lets him decide.

prompt: The distance from the last month of known data to the period being forecast is the forecast's ___, and the range widens as it grows.
hint: One to three months, for Lívia's quarter.

prompt: In your sheet, what is the MAPE of the seasonal naive method over July to December, in percent to one decimal?
hint: =ROUND(AVERAGE(E2:E7),1)

prompt: Why does Lívia test the methods on July to December 2025 rather than going straight to 2026?
hint: Where is the right answer known?

choices.text: Because 2026 has no data at all yet, so no method can produce a forecast for it
choices.why: Every method produces a 2026 forecast from 2025; what is missing is a way to mark it.

choices.text: In the past the right answer is known, so each method's miss can be measured
choices.why: Right: a backtest is the only place a forecasting method can be marked.

choices.text: Because the second half is the hardest part of the year
choices.why: It does hold the season, which makes it a good test, but the reason to test at all is that the answer is known.

choices.text: To show Otávio that 2025 was a good year
choices.why: That is descriptive work, done in lesson 6.

prompt: In the backtest, the growth method used the first half's growth, 5.9%, not the whole year's 5.7%. Why?
hint: What did Lívia pretend the date was?

choices.text: Because a higher growth rate gives the better forecast here
choices.why: The rate was chosen by what was known, not by which result it gave.

choices.text: Because the whole year includes October, which would spoil the test
choices.why: Leaving a bad month out to improve a test is exactly what a backtest must not do.

choices.text: At the end of June, the whole year was not yet known
choices.why: Right: a backtest uses only what was known at the time, or it measures a forecast nobody could have made.

choices.text: Because growth rates are always computed on half years
choices.why: The 2026 forecast uses the whole of 2025, because by January it was known.

prompt: A method forecast 900 for a month in which the actual was 1,000. What is its absolute percentage error, to one decimal?
hint: The error without its sign, divided by the actual.

prompt: The growth method was 6.7% too high in October. What does the lesson conclude from that miss?
hint: What moved in 2025 that the history did not contain?

choices.text: That it is blind to decisions that move the calendar
choices.why: Right: the campaign moved to November, and nothing in the sales history said it would.

choices.text: That the growth method should be dropped in favour of the seasonal naive one
choices.why: Its MAPE is 2.3 against 5.3; one miss does not undo that.

choices.text: That October should be removed from the backtest
choices.why: Removing the month a method fails on makes the test flatter the method.

choices.text: That the first half's growth was computed wrongly
choices.why: The other five months are within 2.4%, which a wrong growth rate would not allow.

prompt: The seasonal naive forecast was below the actual in five months out of six. What is that called, and why does it matter?
hint: Plan stock on it for a year.

choices.text: Noise, and it averages out over the year
choices.why: Noise goes both ways. Misses in one direction add up instead: 5.3% short over the half year.

choices.text: Bias, and it accumulates instead of cancelling
choices.why: Right: stock planned on it runs short month after month.

choices.text: Horizon, because the later months are further from June
choices.why: The horizon is the distance; the direction of the misses is a different property.

choices.text: MAPE, which measures how often a forecast is low
choices.why: MAPE measures the size of the misses without their sign, so it cannot see the direction.

prompt: A method's absolute percentage errors over four months were 4, 2, 6 and 8. What is its MAPE?
hint: The mean of the four.

prompt: A consultant offers Varanda a forecasting model with a MAPE of 4% on July to December 2025. What should Lívia conclude?
hint: Compare it with the baselines on the same months.

choices.text: That it is excellent, because 4% is a small error
choices.why: A MAPE means nothing alone; on these months a formula already does better.

choices.text: That it is worth buying, since it beats the naive method's 15.7%
choices.why: Beating the naive method proves nothing the seasonal methods had not already done.

choices.text: That it is worse than last year's month times growth, at 2.3%
choices.why: Right: a new method has to beat the best baseline on the same months to be worth anything.

choices.text: That MAPE is the wrong measure and the consultant should use another
choices.why: MAPE is fine here; it is the comparison that settles the question.

prompt: Put the steps from a backtest to a range in order.
hint: Pretend, forecast, measure, summarise, apply.
items: Pick a past period and use only the data known before it
Forecast each month of it with each method
Compute each month's absolute percentage error
Average them into a MAPE and check the signs for bias
Forecast the next period with the winner, plus or minus its typical miss
trap: Forecasting the future first and testing afterwards is the tempting order, and it gives a number with no evidence for its range.

prompt: A forecast is 500, and the method's typical miss in its backtest was 4%. What is the low end of the range?
For which of these does a method that copies last year's month have nothing to copy? Choose all that apply.
hint: No history, no last year.

choices.text: A store opened in August
choices.why: Right: it has no last year to repeat.

choices.text: An outdoor-kitchen line launched in March
choices.why: Right: its first months reflect the launch, not a pattern.

choices.text: Garden hoses at a store open for ten years
choices.why: Ten years of history is exactly what the method needs.

choices.text: December at the online shop, open since 2019
choices.why: There are six Decembers to copy.

prompt: Caio ordered few hose reels because the forecast was low, the shelves emptied, and sales came in low. How can Lívia check whether the forecast was really right?
hint: Something the forecast could not influence.

choices.text: Compare the forecast with the month's sales, line by line and store by store
choices.why: The sales were shaped by the forecast through the stock order, so they agree by construction.

choices.text: Look at the days in stock and the visits to the product's page
choices.why: Right: those show the demand the empty shelf hid.

choices.text: Run the same forecast again with more decimal places
choices.why: Precision does not reach the lost sales, which are in no sales record.

choices.text: Ask Caio whether he thinks the forecast was right
choices.why: He saw the same sales, which look like a confirmed forecast.

prompt: What does the lesson give as the sign that a forecasting method has hit a break in the pattern?
hint: 2% becomes 10%.

choices.text: A month with a holiday in it
choices.why: A holiday repeats yearly and the seasonal methods already carry it.

choices.text: A single month with a large miss that has an explanation, such as October
choices.why: One explained miss is an event the method could not see, not a break in the pattern.

choices.text: Errors that jump from small to large, all in one direction
choices.why: Right: the past has stopped describing the future, and the method should be said to have stopped working.

choices.text: A forecast that is higher than last year's actual
choices.why: In a growing company that is ordinary.

prompt: A vendor's demo shows its tool forecasting Varanda's March with a 1% error. What is the first thing Lívia should ask?
hint: One month, chosen by whom?

choices.text: Which algorithm the tool uses
choices.why: Every model is judged the same way whatever it is made of.

choices.text: Whether the tool can draw the forecast as a chart
choices.why: A chart of an untested forecast is still untested.

choices.text: How much a licence costs per user
choices.why: Price matters only once the tool beats what a formula already does.

choices.text: Its MAPE over several months, against the baselines on the same months
choices.why: Right: one month proves little, and a model is only worth its cost if it beats the baseline.

prompt: Which of these should travel with a forecast sent to a director? Choose all that apply.
hint: Number, horizon, range, and what the method cannot see.

choices.text: The range, taken from the method's backtest
choices.why: Right: it says how much weight the number can carry.

choices.text: A note on events the method cannot see, such as a campaign that moved
choices.why: Right: the backtest's worst month says what kind of event that is.

choices.text: The forecast to the nearest real, to show precision
choices.why: A forecast that misses by 2% gains nothing from its last digits, and they suggest a precision it does not have.

choices.text: The period it covers
choices.why: Right: the horizon, without which the range means nothing.

prompt: A simple method that any fancier forecasting method has to beat, such as last year's month times growth, is called a ___.
hint: Machine-learning lesson 2.
